scene.text: Eli checks the clock. 17:59. A coat, a key, one unfinished shift.
Eli checks the clock. 17:59. A coat, a key, one unfinished shift.
The second hand stops. In the other memory, the wall is burned. 18:00.
“I am alive. I came to finish the handover.”
Eli turns to today’s page, not the damaged register from twelve years ago.
He signs his own name. He is here to complete a handover, not to take Gary’s place.
The standby circuit engages. The return lift lights up.
The loading gate is held by pressure, not a lock. Eli turns the bypass wheel.
A hiss, then a clear passage. The service lift begins moving again.
The pipe knocks three times. Eli waits for the needle to fall.
Steam clears from the lower gallery. Someone has left a handprint on the release.
Cold water travels down the glass gauge. The stalled pump catches.
The return lift rises. This is a way back, not another dead end.
Eli braces the inspection bridge. Its far latch finally seats.
The direct return route stays open in both memories.
Three pressure lines settle into the green. The boiler is safe to leave.
A name is scratched under the wheel: GARY — RELEASE FIRST.
Eli signs the present-day duty book. The handwriting is his own.
Twelve years earlier, another signature ends in a torn line.
The public evacuation list says everyone left. One line is suspiciously neat.
Eli opens the inner work ring. The archive can now be reached from either side.
GARY — EVACUATED. The time is earlier than the fire-door release.
Eli crosses out the error. RETURNED TO RELEASE DOORS. STATUS UNCONFIRMED.
“You were still here. I will not write you out again.”
A telephone rings in the empty pantry. Eli lifts the receiver.
Gary, in the memory: “The last door. Do not let it lock.”
Eli: “I heard you. I will leave it open.” The ringing stops.
18:00. Gary pulls the manual release while smoke fills the corridor.
The fire doors open. People run past him toward the stairs. He holds the lever.
The record called him evacuated. This is what it missed.
Eli kneels beside the narrow door gap and sets down the lunchbox.
He slides it through. A hand receives it. No attack. Just a long pause.
Gary: “One more shift?” Eli: “No. This is the handover.”
The roof fans stop fighting the emergency supply. Eli isolates the motor line.
The beacon has its own circuit now, but its final switch is still off.
Water rises through the tower’s sight glass. A float lifts the lower walkway.
There is enough for the plants and enough to keep the return pump running.
Eli waters the three planters, slowly. Leaves lift out of the dust.
The trellis lowers into a bridge. Beyond it, the exterior door can open.
The emergency route drawing ends at a door that was marked sealed.
Gary’s pencil arrow points through it. Eli resets the exterior latch.
The lamp circuit is independent of the building’s main switch.
Eli leaves the final choice at the exit: a lamp can stay on after everyone leaves.
The shutters begin their closing cycle. A warning bell sounds before anything moves.
“Do not wait in the corridor. I have the release.”
The exit is to the right. Run when you are ready.
Eli switches the exit lamp to its independent supply and holds the door.
The waiting figures turn toward the light. One by one, they step outside.
Gary takes his lunchbox and comes last. Eli: “I am leaving you a door.”
The corrected last page reads: EVERYONE HAS LEFT. The lamp stays on.
